name: Adenosine Deaminase Deficiency Severe Combined Immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: None established; diagnosis based on clinical, laboratory, and genetic findings

criteria.description: Severe lymphopenia affecting T, B, and NK cells
Markedly reduced or absent adenosine deaminase enzyme activity in red blood cells or lymphocytes
Pathogenic mutations identified in the ADA gene
Elevated toxic purine metabolites such as deoxyadenosine nucleotides in blood or urine
Recurrent severe infections and failure to thrive in infancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe lymphopenia, ADA enzyme deficiency, and pathogenic ADA gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis confirmed by biochemical and genetic testing; newborn screening may detect early

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe combined T, B, and NK lymphocyte depletion

common.symptomName: Recurrent severe bacterial, viral, and fungal infections

laboratory: Severe lymphopenia (low T, B, NK cells)
Absent or markedly reduced ADA enzyme activity
Elevated deoxyadenosine nucleotides and toxic purine metabolites
imaging: Chest X-ray may show absent thymic shadow
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in ADA gene confirmed by sequencing
other: Newborn screening may detect elevated metabolites or low T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs)

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in RAG1 or RAG2 genes
Absent T and B cells but normal NK cells

redFlags: Severe, recurrent infections in early infancy
Absent thymic shadow on chest imaging
references: Buckley RH. Molecular defects in human severe combined immunodeficiency and approaches to immune reconstitution. Annu Rev Immunol. 2004;22:625-55.
Hirschhorn R. Adenosine deaminase deficiency: clinical presentation and molecular basis. Immunol Allergy Clin North Am. 2001;21(4):715-38.
Notarangelo LD, et al. Primary immunodeficiencies: 2009 update. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2009;124(6):1161-78.
